title: Types Do Not Coerce
goal: Numeric types never convert automatically, and literals without explicit types infer from usage or adopt defaults.

source.attribution: adapted from Day 1 Morning: Primitive Types

sections.text: In languages like Python or C, numbers convert automatically when combined. Rust never converts numeric types implicitly.

sections.caption: Mixing i32 and i64 without casting is error E0308.

sections.text: When you write an integer literal like `10`, Rust infers its type from how it is used. If nothing constrains it, Rust defaults integers to `i32` and floats to `f64`.

sections.caption: Rust infers the type of a from its argument position.

sections.text: To convert between primitive numeric types, use the `as` keyword explicitly. Type casting keeps numeric operations explicit and safe.

explanation: Numeric types never convert automatically, and literals without explicit types infer from usage or adopt defaults.
